src_sentence: In 1868, the British chocolate company Cadbury created Fancy Boxes – a decorated box of chocolates – in the shape of a heart for Valentine's Day. Boxes of filled chocolates quickly became associated with the holiday.
translation: Nel 1868, la ditta di cioccolatini britannica Cadbury creò le Fancy Boxes – una scatola di cioccolatini decorata – a forma di cuore per San Valentino. Le scatole di cioccolatini ripieni divennero rapidamente associate alla festività.

src_sentence: The Valentines honored on February 14 are Valentine of Rome (Valentinus presb. m. Romae) and Valentine of Terni (Valentinus ep. Interamnensis m. Romae).
translation: I santi Valentino onorati il 14 febbraio sono Valentino di Roma (Valentinus presb. m. Romae) e Valentino di Terni (Valentinus ep. Interamnensis m. Romae).

src_sentence: This contrasts with honmei-choko (本命チョコ, lit. "true feeling chocolate"), chocolate given to a loved one. Friends, especially girls, may exchange chocolate referred to as tomo-choko (友チョコ, from 'tomo' meaning "friend").
translation: Ciò contrasta con l'honmei-choko (本命チョコ, letteralmente "cioccolato del vero sentimento"), il cioccolato donato a una persona amata. Gli amici, in particolare le ragazze, possono scambiarsi cioccolato chiamato tomo-choko (友チョコ, da "tomo" che significa "amico").

src_sentence: Valentine's Day customs—sending greeting cards (known as "valentines"), offering confectionery and presenting flowers—developed in early modern England and spread throughout the English-speaking world in the 19th century.
translation: Le usanze di San Valentino – l'invio di biglietti d'auguri (noti come "valentines"), l'offerta di dolci e la presentazione di fiori – si svilupparono nell'Inghilterra della prima età moderna e si diffuse in tutto il mondo anglofono nel XIX secolo.

src_sentence: However, in 2017 and 2018, after a fatwa was widely circulated, the religious police did not prevent Muslims from celebrating the day. In 2018, Sheikh Ahmed Qasim Al-Ghamdi, a Saudi cleric and former president of the Committee for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice, said that Valentine's Day is not haram and is compatible with Islamic values.
translation: Tuttavia, nel 2017 e nel 2018, dopo che una fatwā era stata ampiamente diffusa, la Muṭawwiʿa non impedì ai musulmani di festeggiare la giornata. Nel 2018, lo sceicco Ahmed Qasim Al-Ghamdi, un religioso saudita ed ex presidente del Comitato per la promozione della virtù e la prevenzione del vizio, ha affermato che San Valentino non è haram ed è compatibile con i valori dell'Islam.

src_sentence: The day of love was traditionally March 12, Saint Gregory's day, or February 22, Saint Vincent's Day. The patron of love was Saint Anthony, whose day has been celebrated on June 13.

src_sentence: The celebration of Saint Valentine is not known to have had any romantic connotations until Chaucer's poetry about "Valentine's Day" in the 14th century, some seven hundred years after celebration of Lupercalia is believed to have ceased.
translation: Non risulta che la celebrazione di San Valentino abbia avuto alcuna connotazione romantica fino alla poesia di Geoffrey Chaucer su "San Valentino" nel XIV secolo, circa sette secoli dopo che si ritiene siano cessate le celebrazioni dei Lupercalia.

src_sentence: Fancy Valentines were made with real lace and ribbons, with paper lace introduced in the mid-19th century.

src_sentence: From their survey results, they found three primary reasons: over-commercialization of the holiday, not having a spouse or significant other to celebrate it with, and not being interested in celebrating it.
translation: Dai risultati del loro sondaggio, hanno riscontrato tre ragioni principali: l'eccessiva commercializzazione della festività, il non avere un coniuge o un partner con cui festeggiarla e il non essere interessati a festeggiarla.

src_sentence: In France, a traditionally Catholic country, Valentine's Day is known simply as "Saint Valentin", and is celebrated in much the same way as other Western countries.
translation: In Francia, paese tradizionalmente di Chiesa cattolica, San Valentino è noto semplicemente come "Saint Valentin", e viene celebrato più o meno allo stesso modo degli altri paesi occidentali.

src_sentence: There is an additional embellishment to The Golden Legend, which according to Henry Ansgar Kelly, was added in the 18th century and widely repeated.

src_sentence: As elsewhere, couples exchange gifts, but in some regions, women give a lenço de namorados ("lovers' handkerchief"), which is usually embroidered with love motifs.

src_sentence: Valentine's Day symbols that are used today include the heart-shaped outline, doves, and the figure of the winged Cupid.
translation: I simboli di San Valentino utilizzati oggi includono il profilo a forma di cuore, le colombe e la figura del Cupido alato.

src_sentence: In Ancient Rome, Lupercalia was observed February 13–15 on behalf of Pan and Juno, pagan gods of love, marriage and fertility.
translation: Nell'Antica Roma, i Lupercalia venivano osservati dal 13 al 15 febbraio in onore di Pan e Giunone, divinità del Paganesimo dell'amore, del matrimonio e della fertilità.

src_sentence: Plants and flowers start to grow on this day. It has been celebrated as the day when the first work in the vineyards and in the fields commences.

src_sentence: The first recorded association of Saint Valentine's Day with romantic love is believed to be in the Parliament of Fowls (1382) by Geoffrey Chaucer, a dream vision portraying a parliament for birds to choose their mates.
translation: La prima associazione documentata del giorno di San Valentino con l'amore romantico si ritiene sia ne Il parlamento degli uccelli (1382) di Geoffrey Chaucer, una Visio (letteratura) che ritrae un parlamento in cui gli uccelli scelgono i loro compagni.

src_sentence: In 2019, a survey by the National Retail Federation found that over the previous decade, the percentage of people who celebrate Valentine's Day had declined steadily.

src_sentence: According to findings, Singaporeans are among the biggest spenders on Valentine's Day, with 60% of Singaporeans indicating that they would spend between $100 and $500 during the season leading up to the holiday.
